Impact traces downstream contracts and proves safety facts through existing checks or owned isolated scratch probes. Product edits and external effects require separate authority. Use source/history evidence directly; external How/Why/Arena/Unslop installations are not required.

Principles are contextual references within the authorized scope; fixing a repeated fault stays in task scope and the rest is reported.

Both use the shared selection reference directly without recursively selecting another workflow. Selected methods inherit the task write, evidence and delivery scope.
Keep the declared race rule and exact SHA/method evidence; retry a missing record once; gaps are not passes; stop the remaining workers after a race is decided.

Selection uses Team Up policy only; actual candidate/judge models and independence gaps are reported.
Modes apply per section; reference keeps the qualifications its evidence requires; Unslop is not a second pass; PR writing stays out of scope.
One shared Unslop catalog; rules apply within genre and author voice, and never remove evidence qualifications or exact strings.

Audit Trail activates on explicit request or resume of a selected trail. Its append-only TSV is linked evidence attached to the single Tracking Home, not a second execution-state system. Show Me still owns presentation; Tracking retains commit, code-review, handoff and acceptance policy. Only selected Audit Trail adds an extra required tracking artifact.

Reconcile only the current run's stretches against its workspace-scoped transcript and evidence. Use a different-family read-only reviewer when available; report missing transcript access, independence or review as gaps without substituting self-review or unperformed No flags. Preserve append-only corrections and run ownership. Attention is recorded at checkpoint handoffs, not every progress reply; audit findings feed existing tracking state without a new acceptance gate.

Diagnose is the advisory default; Enforce requires explicit implementation authority and bounded recurring mistake classes. Corrections alone do not trigger edits. Preserve recurrence evidence, structural prevention and real-mistake proof without mandatory rule tables, unrelated repairs or automatic publication. Existing authorization needs no repeated approval.

Worst-case UI data enters the real component through an isolated temporary harness. Product source and live data stay unchanged; retaining fixtures and implementing fixes are separate authorized work. A recreation is not proof of the original component.

Interface explains observed mechanisms without a craft or accessibility verdict. Browser inspection stays read-only; a screenshot supports a qualified reconstruction, not proof of authored CSS, framework identity or accessibility conformance.

All Tickets owns dependency scheduling, fresh workers and merger-validated integration; Implement owns the shared final review, PR and CI cycle. Engineering Principles supplies implementation methods. Local tickets need no external tracker setup. Base resets apply only to worktrees without their own work. The coordinator owns user decisions, including missing test seams.

Interrogate owns independent challenge and verification; Council broadens subjects and retains supported objections and unknowns; Doubt discipline owns context extraction, reconciliation and a three-cycle stop bound. Team Up supplies selected Arena phases and available model selection. Reviewer count follows scope. Review is advisory, not authorization for fixes or publication.

Design Artifact is HTML UI's Artifact mode for standalone visual HTML deliverables and the shared visual-direction reference for Wireframe and Model. Wireframe's low-fidelity contract and Model's fidelity, state and interaction rules stay authoritative when they read it. Its publish offer applies only when Artifact is the selected mode.

Choreograph owns the relationships between two or more animations triggered by the same event: roles, order, overlap, sequence, carry, group interruption and group reduced motion. Animate owns each single animation's decision, properties, curve, duration and exit. Opportunities owns whether motion is warranted, including removing it.
